name: Partial Cubes, Well-Graded Families, and Media
statement: A finite connected graph is a partial cube exactly when it is the one-inclusion graph of a finite well-graded family, and exactly when it is the state graph of a finite medium. In the canonical add/delete medium, reverse-token pairs correspond bijectively to Theta classes; two finite media are isomorphic exactly when their state graphs are isomorphic.
proof: Every graph path in a one-inclusion graph has length at least the Hamming distance, so well-gradedness is exactly isometry in the cube. The set-family representation theorem identifies well-graded families with the canonical reversible add/delete media and reconstructs every finite medium this way. Effective transitions of one reverse-token pair are precisely the edges of one coordinate Theta class; the medium uniqueness theorem gives the final assertion.
